notes:
Segment covers Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Rajasthan in full per SCHEMA/MINISTRIES ownership rules. This is a REPAIR run (r2): a prior attempt at this segment (scratch/states-mp-cg-rj/) went off-task after its context was contaminated by an unrelated relayed message about a site called 'CivLab' and did not produce data/raw/states-mp-cg-rj.json; this run ignores that unrelated message per the repair instructions and completes the assigned research. WebSearch was exhausted for this session (200/200 used by other parallel segments) after 3 initial queries returned no results; all research after that point used WebFetch + curl against the Wikipedia parse API (occasionally rate-limited by concurrent parallel agents; retried) plus stable general knowledge for uncontested structural facts (unicameral legislatures, Article citations). Key verified facts: MP Governor Mangubhai C. Patel's incumbency was reconfirmed via a Wikipedia revision updated 7 September 2026 (no 2025-26 change). CG cabinet reflects the 20 Aug 2025 reshuffle (3 new ministers replacing Brijmohan Agrawal, who left 19 Jun 2024 for the Lok Sabha). RJ Assembly party strength was taken from the current infobox (BJP 118/INC 67) rather than the as-declared 2023 result (BJP 115/INC 70/Others 15) because the former purports to reflect post-by-election reality; the 'Others' 2-seat detail (a party labelled 'Shiv Sena' in the source, which is unusual for Rajasthan) could not be independently confirmed and may be a source/extraction error - flagged low confidence on that specific line only. GAPS / lower-confidence areas, consistent with the precedent set by the sibling states-mh-gj-ga.json segment: (1) Individual Wikipedia URLs were verified only for top office-holders (Governors, CMs, Deputy CMs, Speakers, LoPs) - not for the ~64 rank-and-file cabinet/MoS ministers across the three states, to avoid inventing unverified links; a follow-up pass should add these. (2) Constituencies were sourced for all 14 Chhattisgarh ministers but could not be confirmed for individual Madhya Pradesh or Rajasthan ministers without inventing them, so are omitted there. (3) Chief Secretary and DGP appointment dates for all three states, and the exact current heads of the Madhya Pradesh/Chhattisgarh/Rajasthan State Human Rights Commissions and the Chhattisgarh State Election Commission, could not be confirmed and are recorded as low confidence or omitted rather than guessed. (4) Ramnivas Rawat's current portfolio in the Madhya Pradesh cabinet is uncertain: Wikipedia's ministry table shows he left the Forest and Environment portfolio on 4 Dec 2024, but he still appears as a minister in the district-wise minister list; flagged low confidence rather than guessing a portfolio. (5) Municipal corporation lists (MP 16, CG 14, RJ 10) were sourced from a single Wikipedia summary table and not cross-checked against each state's Urban Development Department list; mayors/administrators were not resolved for any corporation given time constraints - a follow-up pass should add these plus each corporation's official website. (6) Legislative Council: none of the three states has a Vidhan Parishad (all unicameral), so no st-<code>-legislative-council entities were created, per schema. (7) State Election Commission head for Chhattisgarh specifically could not be found.

--- Adversarial verification pass (2026-09-25) ---
Structural check (python): 0 duplicate IDs, 0 dangling parentId/orgId/relation references, all kind/sector/rank values in schema vocab, all entities/positions carry confidence+sources. Coverage counts (64 entities / 96 positions / 76 relations) verified internally consistent with the brief's stated composition (3 states, 3 state_governments, 3 councils, 3 legislatures, 12 commissions [SEC/PSC/Lokayukta/SHRC x3], 40 municipal corporations; 3 governors, 3 CMs, 6 deputy CMs, 61 state ministers, 3 speakers, 3 deputy speakers [all vacant/unconfirmed], 3 LoPs, 3 chief secretaries, 11 head_of_agency; 6 appoints + 67 advises_appointment + 3 accountable_to relations). Fresh 2025-2026 web verification (WebSearch budget was exhausted session-wide, so verification used WebFetch against Wikipedia biography pages plus Google News RSS) confirmed as correct: all 3 Governors, all 3 CMs, all 6 Deputy CMs, all 3 Speakers, all 3 LoPs, MP/CG Chief Secretaries, MP/CG/RJ DGPs (1 spelling fix), all 11 CG cabinet ministers with portfolios, all 29 MP ministers/MoS with portfolios (cross-checked against the live Mohan_Yadav_ministry Wikipedia page), and the RJ Assembly party-strength breakdown including the previously-flagged 'Shiv Sena 2 seats' line. Found and corrected 4 stale/wrong facts (see verification.corrections): RJ Chief Secretary's start date, CG DGP name spelling, and two commission chairs (MP Lokayukta, RJ PSC Chairman) whose file holders had been superseded by 2024/2026 appointments not reflected in the sources the original run used. Ramnivas Rawat's MP cabinet portfolio remains genuinely unresolved: a fresh search surfaced a conflicting/undated 'new Forest and Environment Minister' headline alongside an ongoing Vijaypur seat legal dispute, so the existing LOW CONFIDENCE flag was left in place rather than overwritten with an unconfirmed claim. Not independently re-verified in this pass (time-boxed): MP/RJ State Election Commissioners, MP PSC Chairman, CG/MP/RJ State Human Rights Commission heads, municipal corporation mayors/administrators, and per-minister Wikipedia URLs for rank-and-file ministers — these carry the same gaps/medium-or-omitted confidence the original run already flagged.
